title: Boundary matching covers imply local acyclic fibration
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves and [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] for simplicial sets. Use [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps] for the homotopy-group and local-map conventions. For $V\in\mathcal C$, put $h_V(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(W,V)$. The simplex $\Delta^n$ is represented by $[n]$, its boundary $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of its proper faces (empty when $n=0$), and $\Lambda_i^n$ is the union of the faces other than face $i$, for $n\ge1$ and $0\le i\le n$. Let $F,G:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$ be objectwise Kan simplicial presheaves: for every $V$, each map from a horn $\Lambda_i^n$ to $F(V)$ or $G(V)$ extends to $\Delta^n$, for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. A map $f:F\to G$ is a local Kan fibration if every commutative square from $h_V\times\Lambda_i^n\to h_V\times\Delta^n$ to $f$ has fillers after restriction along every arrow in some covering sieve of $V$; the fillers need not agree for different arrows. For objectwise Kan $F,G$, call $f$ a local weak equivalence if it induces an isomorphism on the associated sheaves of $\pi_0$ and, for each $V\in\mathcal C$, $x\in F(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, an isomorphism on the associated sheaves on $\mathcal C/V$ of $\pi_m(F|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(G|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$, where $\mathcal C/V$ has the induced topology. For $n\geq0$, define $\widetilde M_nF(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}}(\partial\Delta^n,F(V))$ and define $\widetilde M_nG$ similarly. If, for every $n$, the natural map $F_n\longrightarrow\widetilde M_nF\times_{\widetilde M_nG}G_n$ is a generalized cover [def-cbc-generalized-cover], then $f$ is both a local Kan fibration and a local weak equivalence. In degree zero the hypothesis is local surjectivity of $F_0\to G_0$.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, Proposition 3.2 and reformulation (3.4), printed pp. 7-8, converse direction; read online, archival local copy WANTED. No corresponding Stacks tag.

proof.text: A section of $\widetilde M_nF\times_{\widetilde M_nG}G_n$ at $V$ is a boundary square $(a,b)$, with $a:\partial\Delta^n\to F(V)$, $b:\Delta^n\to G(V)$ and $f_Va=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$. Explicitly, an $n$-simplex $z$ of $Z$ corresponds to the map sending $\alpha:[q]\to[n]$ to $Z(\alpha)(z)$; evaluation at the identity is inverse. The matching map therefore sends $z$ to $(z|_{\partial\Delta^n},f_Vz)$. By [def-cbc-generalized-cover], the hypothesis supplies a covering sieve on which every such square has strict fillers. We may work with these objectwise squares: a map $h_V\times K\to F$ is determined by $a:K\to F(V)$, and its value on $(u:W\to V,k)$ is $F(u)(a(k))$. For $n=0$, the boundary is empty, so the same hypothesis is exactly local surjectivity on vertices.

source.place: Section 3, definition of generalized cover and equation (3.4), printed pp. 7-8; simplex evaluation written out.

proof.text: Fix a finite inclusion $A\subseteq B$ and a square $a:A\to F(V)$, $b:B\to G(V)$ over $f$. By [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], this inclusion is a composite of finitely many single boundary attachments: only finitely many nondegenerate simplices of $B$ lie outside $A$, and the coproduct of cells in each dimension can be attached one cell at a time. Write the resulting filtration as $A=B_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq B_N=B$. Let $R_j$ be the sieve of arrows $u:W\to V$ where the restricted square has a filler on $B_j$. It is a sieve since fillers restrict further, and $R_0$ is maximal. If $R_j$ covers, choose a partial filler for each $u$ in $R_j$. The next cell gives one boundary square over $W$, so Step 1 gives a covering sieve $T_u$ on $W$ where this partial filler extends to $B_{j+1}$; the boundary agreement glues the cell to the partial filler by the pushout property. Thus $T_u\subseteq u^*R_{j+1}$. Covering sieves are upward closed: if $T\subseteq T'$ and $T$ covers, the pullback of $T'$ along any arrow of $T$ is maximal, so transitivity makes $T'$ cover. Hence $u^*R_{j+1}$ covers for every $u$ in $R_j$, and transitivity makes $R_{j+1}$ cover. Finite induction gives $R_N$ covering. This proves local strict lifting against every finite simplicial inclusion, including an empty domain; no agreement of fillers for different arrows is needed.

source.place: Proposition 7.2, first implication, and the finite boundary-cell argument of Corollary 6.14, printed pp. 14-15; explicit induction with covering sieves.

proof.text: For each $n\ge1$ and $0\le i\le n$, the horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\subseteq\Delta^n$ is an inclusion of finite simplicial sets: the nondegenerate simplices of $\Delta^n$ are its strictly increasing vertex strings, of which there are finitely many, and the horn is a union of faces. Step 2 therefore gives local strict fillers for every horn square. This is precisely the local Kan fibration condition of [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps], also when $n=1$.

source.place: Proposition 7.2, first paragraph of proof, printed p. 15.

proof.text: Every component of $G(V)$ has a vertex representative $y$. The degree-zero instance of Step 1 locally lifts $y$, proving local surjectivity of $\pi_0F\to\pi_0G$. For local injectivity, let vertices $x_0,x_1$ of $F(V)$ have the same component after applying $f$. By the definition of components, a finite zigzag of edges in $G(V)$ joins $f(x_0)$ to $f(x_1)$. Glue the corresponding copies of $\Delta^1$ end to end, allowing either orientation, to form a finite simplicial interval $I$ with distinct abstract endpoints $v_0,v_1$. There is a map $I\to G(V)$ realizing that zigzag. The map $\{v_0,v_1\}\to F(V)$ given by $x_0,x_1$ forms a square for Step 2. Its local fillers are zigzags in $F$ joining the restricted vertices, so their components become equal locally. A zero-length zigzag is already equality of the image vertices and may be represented by one degenerate edge, so this case is included.

source.place: Theorem 6.15(a), first implication, printed p. 14, degree-zero local bijectivity; strict lifting specializes its homotopy-lifting argument.

proof.text: Fix $V$, $x\in F(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$. On any object $u:W\to V$ of the slice, put $x_W=F(u)x$. By [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps], every class of $\pi_m(G(W),f(x_W))$ is represented by a map $b:\Delta^m\to G(W)$ constant with value $f(x_W)$ on $\partial\Delta^m$. Prescribe the constant map $x_W$ on that boundary and apply Step 1. Each local strict lift is a pointed representative in $F$, whose image is exactly $b$ on restriction. Thus the homotopy-group presheaf map on $\mathcal C/V$ is locally surjective. The covering sieve on $W$ is a covering sieve in this slice at $u$, by the definition of the induced topology.

source.place: Theorem 6.15(a), first implication and its sphere test, printed p. 14; Definition 6.6 and Proposition 6.9 for slice basepoints.

proof.text: For injectivity, take pointed representatives $a_0,a_1:\Delta^m\to F(W)$ whose image classes are equal. Equality in the quotient of [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps] means a finite zigzag of relative cylinder homotopies in $G(W)$ from $f(a_0)$ to $f(a_1)$. Form $L$ by gluing one copy of $\Delta^m\times\Delta^1$ for each homotopy along the adjacent full endpoint copies of $\Delta^m$, in the direction specified by that zigzag. Let $A\subseteq L$ be the union of the first and last endpoint copies and all copies of $\partial\Delta^m\times\Delta^1$. The homotopies glue to $h:L\to G(W)$. Define $a:A\to F(W)$ to be $a_0,a_1$ on the outer endpoints and the constant $x_W$ on every boundary prism. These prescriptions agree on intersections because both representatives and every homotopy have constant boundary. Thus $f_Wa=h|_A$. The products are finite by [lem-cbc-finite-simplicial-product]. Their finite glued union $L$ is finite: each nondegenerate image simplex comes from a nondegenerate simplex in some prism, since degeneracies remain degenerate under every simplicial map. Its subcomplex $A$ is finite too. A degenerate simplex $z$ in $L$ can be written $z=s_i y$ (factor its noninjective simplex operator through an elementary surjection). Then $y=d_i z$ lies in $A$ whenever $z$ does, since $A$ is closed under faces. Thus a nondegenerate simplex of $A$ remains nondegenerate in $L$. For a zero-length zigzag use a single constant cylinder; the image endpoint maps then coincide. We have constructed a finite inclusion $A\subseteq L$ with a strict square over $f$.

source.place: Theorem 6.15(a), first implication and its relative homotopy test, printed p. 14; Section 2, definition of pointed homotopy classes, printed p. 3. Explicit finite zigzag version avoids needing transitivity of single homotopies.

proof.text: Apply Step 2 to the finite square constructed in Step 6. On every arrow of a covering sieve of $W$, a filler $L\to F$ restricts to the prescribed outer representatives and the constant basepoint on all boundary prisms. Its restrictions to the individual prisms are relative cylinder homotopies, in the specified orientations, joining those representatives by a finite zigzag in $F$. Their pointed classes are therefore equal by the quotient relation of [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps]. This proves local injectivity at every object of $\mathcal C/V$. All basepoints are restrictions of $x$, and naturality gives $f(x_W)=f(x)|_W$, so no basepoint-change isomorphism is being assumed.

source.place: Theorem 6.15(a), first implication, homotopy-group injectivity test, printed p. 14; finite zigzag lifted strictly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] on $\mathcal C$ to the component map, using the two local conditions proved in Step 4. It yields an isomorphism on the associated component sheaves. For every $V$, $x\in F(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, the slice $\mathcal C/V$ is a small category, and its induced topology (a sieve on $u:W\to V$ covers when the sieve of underlying arrows covers $W$) satisfies the maximality, pullback and transitivity axioms because those of $J$ do. The pointed homotopy-class map $\pi_m(F|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(G|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$, $u\mapsto(\pi_m(F(W),x_W)\to\pi_m(G(W),f(x_W)))$ with restriction by postcomposition as in [def-cbc-local-simplicial-presheaf-maps], is a map of set-valued presheaves on $\mathcal C/V$. Steps 5 and 7, applied at every object $u$ of $\mathcal C/V$, give exactly its local surjectivity and local injectivity for this induced topology. So [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection], applied on the site $\mathcal C/V$, makes its associated-sheaf map an isomorphism. Thus $f$ is a local weak equivalence in the sense of the statement. Together with Step 3 this proves both conclusions. The assumed objectwise Kan hypotheses give the specified pointed homotopy-class sets their usual homotopy-group meaning. No objectwise fibration hypothesis on $f$ or enough-points hypothesis on the site has been used.

source.place: Lemma 6.8 and Proposition 6.9, printed p. 12, and Theorem 6.15(a), first implication, printed p. 14; DHI Proposition 3.2 and equation (3.4).

lean.statement: theorem local_acyclic_of_matching_cover {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ SSet.{max u w}) (hF : ∀ V : C, SSet.KanComplex (F.obj (op V))) (hG : ∀ V : C, SSet.KanComplex (G.obj (op V))) (f : F ⟶ G) (hcover : ∀ n : ℕ, Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J (relativeBoundaryMatchingMap f n)) : IsLocalKanFibration J f ∧ IsLocalWeakEquivalence J f
